chapter: Europe tours, Birdland memories and closing
title: A miserable two weeks opposite Willis Jackson
summary: Cobb and Jackson follow each other on stage with the same arrangements, he fumes and tap dances to compensate, and he demands the scores from his arrangers afterward.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: Oh, I see.
How in the hell you going to get by with after that. Something Willis that? I had to go and tap dance out there. That some Jackson wasn't doing, dancing, really (inaudible), tap dancceer.
Now, they've done this before the two of you went in together.
Huh?
They'd given you these arrangements, not knowing that the two of you would be playing opposite one another?
That was the general idea, but we met on this occasion, and George is up there, one of the guilty parties, playing piano for me.
Well, I mean and Duvivier did (inaudible) played the same thing?
I'm telling you -- had the same -- I couldn't believe it. I said, 'Hell, he's playing the same thing I'm about to play.'
(Laughter)

I was (inaudible). I was so mad, and I got provoked, and, you know, I don't usually get provoked. I'm a pretty good guy, but I turned redder than a beet in the face there and I'm ready to cuss everybody out. And I'm fighting playing this, and I got to go back and think what the hell I can do. And I can't talk to Willis because when I'm on, he's off. When he's off, I'm on. How you going to talk to him? You don't have time to say nothing.
Just listen to what he play.
(Laughter)
In the next set try to beat him to it. That's all you can do.
You must have --
But, man, I had a miserable two weeks in there with that.
And two whole weeks?
Two weeks.
You should have made those guys (inaudible) sit down and write arrangements every night.
(Simultaneous remarks)
I go in like two weeks at a time in there, you know, and I'm telling you.
(Inaudible). That is awful, isn't it?

The only thing George Now didn't do for him was the Ellington medley, and he couldn't do it for him because the way it was, Willis couldn't have done it because he didn't have the same instrumentation I had for what I was going to do. Oh, my God. That is miserable.
Yeah, that's --
Those guys must have been very embarrassed, weren't they?
(Inaudible) God bless Reuben Phillips, so -- he's dead now, but I had to tell him. I told George

Duvivier (inaudible), I said, "Man, anytime you make another arrangement for me, give me the score. Now, if I got to pay for it, give me the whole works because I don't want nobody else playing the same thing I'm playing. I don't want to run into this hassle anymore." (inaudible).
It's ridiculous.
Sure, it's ridiculous.
I'm surprised George, you know, George is usually (inaudible).
Man, they were making money. That's what they was doing. Now, who else had it, I don't know. I didn't cross them. But I crossed Willis Jackson in Birdland because we played on the same bill together.
